Of course. Here is the year-over-year (YoY) U.S. core inflation rate from January 2015 to December 2016.

This data represents the 12-month percentage change in the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPI-U), excluding the volatile food and energy components. The data is sourced from the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS).

| Month | 2015 Rate | 2016 Rate |
|:---|:---:|:---:|
| January | 1.6% | 2.2% |
| February | 1.7% | 2.3% |
| March | 1.8% | 2.2% |
| April | 1.8% | 2.1% |
| May | 1.7% | 2.2% |
| June | 1.8% | 2.2% |
| July | 1.8% | 2.2% |
| August | 1.8% | 2.3% |
| September | 1.9% | 2.2% |
| October | 1.9% | 2.1% |
| November | 2.0% | 2.1% |
| December | 2.1% | 2.2% |
